props.gloss_en: hide: [one who carries it out is liable for] enough to make an amulet
[bracketed in the printed text] one who tans hide -- how much? no different [enough for an amulet]
one who carries out hide to tan it -- how much? no different [enough for an amulet]
one who carries out hide not to tan it -- how much? no different [enough for an amulet]: tanned and untanned hide share one measure
the whitener, the comber, the dyer and the spinner: the measure is double the full width of the sit
and the weaver of two threads: the measure is double the full width of the sit
evidently: since it stands to be spun, its measure is as spun
here too: since it stands to be tanned, its measure is as tanned
the baraita: one who carries out soaked herbs -- enough to dye with them a sample for the ira
the mishna on unsoaked herbs: nutshells and pomegranate peels, safflower and madder -- enough to dye with them a small cloth for a hair-net
Rabba bar Avuh: because a person does not trouble to soak herbs to dye with them a sample for the ira
the mishna: garden seeds [before sowing] -- less than a dried fig
R' Yehuda ben Beteira: five [seeds]
the mishna [after sowing]: manure and fine sand -- enough to fertilize a cabbage stalk; the words of R' Akiva
and the Sages say: enough to fertilize a leek
Rav Pappa: this where it is sown, that where it is not sown -- because a person does not trouble to carry out a single seed for sowing
the Sages agree with R' Shimon that one who carries out waste water to the public domain -- its measure is a quarter-log
R' Yirmeya: waste water is fit for kneading clay
the baraita: clay -- enough to make the mouth of a crucible
there too as we said: because a person does not trouble to knead clay to make the mouth of a crucible
there are three hides: matza, chifa and diftera. Matza -- as it sounds: not salted, not floured, not galled
chifa -- salted, not floured, not galled
diftera -- salted and floured, not galled
and its [matza's] measure? Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda taught: enough to wrap a small weight in it
and how much [is the small weight]? Abaye: a quarter of a quarter of Pumbedita['s measure]
and chifa's measure? as we learned: hide -- enough to make an amulet
and diftera's measure? enough to write a bill of divorce on it
there [the small-weight measure] is in [the state of] bishula
the garment: three by three, for midras
the sack: four by four
the hide: five by five
a mat: six by six -- whether for midras or for the dead
the garment, the sack and the hide: as the measure for impurity, so the measure for carrying out
that [Tosefta] is of kortovela
